terra.problem: Papa Dorin comments on how he is telling the passage when he says he is not going to joke.
It says the careful work makes the idols a bad idea. The passage identifies the making of idols as sin, not the skill of the craftsmen.
The passage does not say the four things are gone before anyone can grab them.
“Long before” adds a length of time the passage does not give.
The fox punchline makes light of the violent judgment being described.
“I won't add a reason the text doesn't give” comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage.
The smile comparison implies an unmentioned reaction from God and uses it for a joke.
The explanation that Sheol is the place of the dead needs a supporting reference outside this passage.
The schedule punchline has no clear connection to the king or the wind, so it does not pass the joke logic test.
The passage says the wind will come and the fountain and spring will dry up, but does not explicitly say the wind dries them up.
The spring is not the one thing that does not hold up. The fountain also fails, and the treasury is plundered.
The passage does not mention sheep, so it does not establish that they are safe.
The heavy description follows in the same verse, not in the verse that follows.
“I'll just say this part plainly” comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage.
“I won't add another” comments on what Papa Dorin chooses to add to the passage.
The final sentence comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage instead of explaining the answer.
